children: Shares gain as UBS maintains a positive view on the bank ahead of its September-quarter results
Shares of HDFC Bank edged higher on 23 September after UBS reiterated its ‘Buy’ call on the stock, with investors also focusing on the lender’s upcoming September-quarter results.
The stock was trading 0.41 per cent higher at Rs 741.65 around 12:20 pm on the National Stock Exchange, after opening at Rs 735.65. It touched an intraday high of Rs 742.80 and a low of Rs 734.00.
The bank’s shares have remained in focus amid developments around its leadership transition and expectations from its financial performance for the September quarter.
HDFC Bank’s board will meet on 17 October to consider the unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and half-year ended 30 September 2026.
The bank’s trading window will remain closed from 24 September to 19 October in connection with the results.

In the June quarter, HDFC Bank reported a net profit of Rs 19,059.72 crore, up 4.98 per cent year-on-year, while net interest income rose 6.7 per cent to Rs 33,534 crore. Gross non-performing assets stood at 1.17 per cent and net non-performing assets at 0.41 per cent.

The September-quarter results come at a significant point for the bank as managing director and chief executive officer Sashidhar Jagdishan is set to complete his current term on 26 October and has decided not to seek reappointment.
The Reserve Bank of India is considering Anup Bagchi for the chief executive position, with the leadership transition remaining an important factor for investors tracking the bank’s outlook.
The upcoming results are expected to provide investors with an update on loan growth, asset quality, margins and profitability as the bank moves through the leadership transition.
